note: Per-million-token USD rates for Gemini, Claude, and GPT models reachable from ADK agents (native Gemini backend, plus Claude/GPT via ADK's LiteLlm integration -- see google-adk's models/lite_llm.py). Historically Gemini-only (hence the filename/loader name -- kept for now, see _pricing.py's module docstring); Phase 2 W3 added Claude and current-generation GPT entries plus a zero-cost entry for local/self-hosted models (Phase 3 B1: local-model zero-cost pricing now requires the caller to opt in via ADK_TRACEGAUGE_ASSUME_LOCAL -- see the __local_zero_cost__ entry's own note and _pricing.py's module docstring for why: Ollama Cloud, a real paid product, shares the identical ollama_chat//ollama/ LiteLlm prefix as local Ollama). Prices change without notice -- verify against each entry's source_url before relying on a number for a real budget decision. Standard (interactive/online) tier only -- no Batch API pricing (ADK's live-agent plugin path never issues Batch API calls, confirmed by source grep of google-adk's models/plugins modules; a batch call is a separate async job-submission API that never flows through BasePlugin.after_model_callback). Text/image/video input rate only -- several vendors price audio input separately (typically higher); audio calls are priced at the text rate here, which under-charges audio-heavy invocations. schema_version 2 added optional per-model long-context tiering (see 'long_context_threshold_tokens'/'long_context_model_key') -- verified P0 fix, Phase 2 W1. schema_version 3 adds optional 'promo_until' (ISO date) + 'standard_rate' ({input_usd_per_mtok, output_usd_per_mtok}) for time-limited promotional entries -- see _pricing.py's resolve_model/effective_prices, which automatically switch a promotional entry to its standard_rate once promo_until has passed, no manual table edit required (Phase 3 B2).

cache_multipliers._note: This ONE global read-multiplier applies to every model in the table -- tes.cost.compute_turn_cost (tracegauge's shared cost engine) has no per-model cache-multiplier override, so a vendor whose real cache-read discount differs from 0.1x cannot be added here without silently mispricing its cache hits. Gemini's default (automatic/implicit) context caching bills only a read-time discount at 0.1x the model's fresh input rate -- verified per-model against ai.google.dev's published cached-input rates (every model checked, including the >200k long-context tiers, divides out to exactly 0.1x of that tier's own input rate; re-verified 2026-08-14 across 10 models). Claude's prompt-caching cache-read rate is ALSO exactly 0.1x of base input on every current model, per platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing (fetched 2026-08-14, e.g. Opus 5: $0.50 cache-hit / $5.00 base input = 0.1x). OpenAI's CURRENT (GPT-5.x) generation is ALSO 0.1x on every model checked (developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, fetched 2026-08-14, e.g. gpt-5.1: $0.125 cached / $1.25 input = 0.1x) -- this is why Phase 2 W3 added the GPT-5.x family. OpenAI's GPT-4/o-series generation does NOT share this ratio (observed 0.25x on gpt-4.1, 0.5x on gpt-4o and o1) and was deliberately NOT added to this table for that reason -- adding it here would silently under-price any cached call on those models by 2.5x-5x. Register those (or any other off-ratio vendor) via the ADK_TRACEGAUGE_PRICE_TABLE env var override instead, which lets you supply your own cache_multipliers alongside your own models. There is no cache-write surcharge and no cache_creation token field surfaced through ADK's plugin path for any provider (Gemini has none natively; ADK's LiteLlm bridge normalizes OpenAI/Anthropic cache-hit fields into the same cache-READ shape as Gemini's cached_content_token_count but does not surface a separate cache-WRITE token count anywhere adk-tracegauge's plugin can capture it -- see _plugin.py/_store.py), so write multipliers are 0 by design for every entry, not a placeholder. cache_read billing correctness also depends on prompt_token_count already including cached tokens (so fresh_tokens = prompt_token_count - cache_read is not double-billing) -- confirmed directly from the installed google-genai SDK's GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata docstring: 'prompt_token_count ... When cached_content is set, this also includes the number of tokens in the cached content.'
